Subject: [P0] Elevated 95th/99th tail latency observed / token prefetch cache regression

Team —

Seeing a regression in the token prefetch cache rollout that was pushed overnight. Metrics: 95th p99 token latency for hosted/generation endpoints in us-west rose ~2.5x starting ~07:45 UTC, with a correlated uptick in request timeouts and a small spike in 502s. Affected tenants include a subset of long-sequence customers — Crestwell is in the sampling.

Initial triage: rollback flag available; kernel and runtime remain stable; root cause appears to be a prefetch eviction threshold that was too aggressive for long-sequence workloads. Engineers are preparing a targeted rollback to the previous cache behavior. Estimated mitigation ETA: 20-30 minutes if we push rollback now.

Attachments: ops-log-snippet.txt (500 lines, truncated)

Can someone own customer comms? We should get a short advisory out to affected customers and update the status page.

— Logan (on-call)
SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Hosted API advisory: elevated tail latency impacting some long-sequence workloads — immediate advisory draft

Simon / Crestwell Ops team —

We wanted to let you know we are seeing elevated tail latency for hosted generation endpoints that may affect longer-context requests. Our SRE team has identified a regression introduced by a token prefetch cache change rolled last night and is rolling back that change to restore prior cache behavior.

What we know now:
- Impact: increased 95th/99th latency and a small uptick in request errors for some long-sequence requests.
- Scope: limited subset of hosted customers experiencing long sequences; Crestwell observed elevated tails in your calls starting ~07:45 UTC.
- Mitigation: rolling back the prefetch cache change; estimated mitigation ETA 20–30 minutes.
- Workaround: reducing max_context or switching to a lower sequence window temporarily can reduce error rate while we finish rollback.

We plan to post a brief update on our status page when rollback begins and another when the change is reverted. We will follow with a postmortem within 72 hours outlining root cause and corrective actions.

Draft status page text (internal):
"Hosted API — Elevated tail latency due to token prefetch cache regression. Engineering rollback in progress (ETA ~30m). Customers may see increased latency or errors for long-context requests. Full update to follow."

Please confirm if this messaging is OK to send to Crestwell (and to post). Marcus / Laura / Logan — any edits?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
